conviction_note: I found no unpriced company-level number. The evidence is a known Q1 beat habit (guide reaffirmed six and a half weeks into the quarter), a QBO price rise from 1 Aug, a few weak positive SMB and lending proxies, a stock already de-rated 9% in five days with upside skew paid, and against all that a street FY27 EPS sitting about 2% above the guide top, which a reaffirm-only would disappoint. Net that is p_up 55 on an abs move of 8.5 (implied 8.23, own median 5.03, one -20% print in the last seven), so (2*0.55-1)*8.5 = +0.85. The findings sum to +0.9. The two measurements agree because nothing decisive was found.
bar: Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 2026-10-31) company guide: revenue $4,294-4,313M (+11%), GAAP op income $716-729M, non-GAAP op income $902-915M, non-GAAP EPS $2.44-2.48, now on a basis that includes about $521M of SBC. Set 2026-08-25 and reaffirmed at the 2026-09-17 Investor Day (https://finviz.com/news/393199/intuit-hosts-investor-day-reaffirms-first-quarter-and-fiscal-2027-guidance). Consensus: revenue $4.30B and EPS $2.47, whisper $2.59, from Earnings Whispers 2026-11-11 (https://finviz.com/news/421347/intuits-first-test-after-its-growth-reset-hinges-on-quickbooks-customer-momentum). KeyCorp has $2.48. Chartmill's $2.71/$4.391B looks stale on the old ex-SBC basis and is disregarded. FY27 guide: revenue $23,279-23,512M (+9-10%) and non-GAAP EPS $22.88-23.12, against a street FY EPS of $23.49 per Earnings Whispers. The bar is sourced to the company guide plus two estimate sources that agree.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 8.0M shares, roughly 3.0% of shares outstanding, with 2.2 days to cover and up about 10% month on month (equibles summary, short-volume data dated 2026-11-06, https://equibles.com/stocks/intu/shortinterest). The 2026-09-30 settlement was 7.3M shares and 1.8 days (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/intu/short-interest/). Not a crowded short. The baseline skew_25d is -10.85 vol points: call IV is above put IV, so upside is paid. Put/call open interest is 0.54. The front-expiry straddle implies 8.23%. The stock fell 5-6% on 2026-11-17 with its sector down 3.84%, and the reports found no company-specific catalyst (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/market-movers/262309589-market-movers-intu-20261117, https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Intuit+Slides+Ahead+of+Earnings+as+Investors+Reassess+Growth+Outlook). The stock is -9.05% over 5 days, -12.83% over 20 days and -54% from its 52-week high, and sits near the $303 it closed at on 2026-09-18 after the Investor Day downgrade.

findings.finding: Intuit reaffirmed its Q1 guide ($4,294-4,313M revenue, $2.44-2.48 non-GAAP EPS) on 2026-09-17, about seven weeks into a quarter that ends 2026-10-31. The last Q1 (FY26) printed $3,885M revenue, a $126M beat on consensus (about 3.4%), and the stock rose +4.03%. A beat of 1-2% on revenue against the $4.30B consensus is the likely print; the whisper ($2.59 against $2.47) already prices part of it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 (2025-11-20): revenue beat consensus by about $126M, FY guide reiterated, stock +4.03%. Q4 FY26 (2026-08-25): EPS $4.03 vs $3.59 and revenue $4.35B vs $4.27B, but the guide was weak; the stock was -11.8% premarket and closed -3.24%. Beats on this name are paid only when the guide holds.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the whisper is 12 cents (about 5%) above the $2.47 consensus. If the market expected a beat as large as last Q1's 3.4%, revenue consensus would sit above the guide top of $4.313B. It sits at $4.30B, inside the range.
findings.independence: The FY26 Q1 beat-and-reiterate record is in https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20316423 (2025-11-20) and is a separate document. The EPS whisper is at https://finviz.com/news/421347/intuits-first-test-after-its-growth-reset-hinges-on-quickbooks-customer-momentum.

findings.finding: QuickBooks Online list prices for Essentials, Plus and Advanced rose for renewals on or after 2026-08-01, so all three months of Q1 carry the increase (new subscribers keep their old price for six months). Free, Lite, Ledger and Simple Start were unchanged. This supports Online Ecosystem ARPC (+15% last year) against a 3% paying-customer growth rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pricing-led QBO growth with weak customer adds was sold on 2026-08-25: QBO Accounting revenue rose 20% while total online paying customers grew 3%, and the stock fell as analysts focused on the customer count (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/intu-stock-plunges-q4-results-wall-street-divided-growth-foundations/cZYNMHaRJY1).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The increase was announced in June, before the 2026-08-25 guide, so it sits inside the guided range. What is not known is whether it cost customers, which would show up in the paying-customer count. Hence the small size and the two-sided range.
findings.independence: Third-party price detail (Plus $99 to $140, Advanced $200 to $340; not confirmed on Intuit's own page) is at https://www.certumsolutions.com/library/quickbooks-price-increase-august-2026. It rests on the same announcement.

findings.finding: Intuit's own QuickBooks Small Business Index (US firms with 1-9 employees) shows average real monthly revenue per business up 1.68% m/m in September and 2.60% m/m in October 2026, with October revenue up in all eight regions. Employment fell 0.14% (-18,700 jobs) in October and fell in 10 of 12 sectors in September. That is a mild tailwind for payments and transaction volume and a mild headwind for payroll per-employee revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to this index. Online payments volume has grown near 30% a quarter, according to the 2026-11-11 Earnings Whispers preview.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a published monthly series that few previews cite. If it were priced, previews would quote the payments-volume read-across, and the 2026-11-17 coverage instead blamed 'small-business health' worries for the drop. It is a macro-to-company proxy built on Intuit's own customer data, not a reported metric.
findings.independence: The September data is at https://quickbooks.intuit.com/r/small-business-data/index/october-2026/, from the same publisher. BILL's payments read (next finding) is a separate source pointing the same way.

findings.finding: BILL Holdings' fiscal Q1 2027 (September quarter, reported about 2026-11-06) showed total payment volume of $102B, up 14% YoY, and core revenue up 14%. SMB payment activity held up through the September quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of INTU reacting to BILL prints.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer reporting after Intuit last spoke (2026-09-17). It is an industry proxy with no stated link to QuickBooks volumes. If it had moved expectations, Intuit revenue consensus would have moved off $4.30B, and it has not.
findings.independence: The QuickBooks Small Business Index revenue rise points the same way (https://quickbooks.intuit.com/r/small-business-data/index/november-2026/). The call summary is at https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-bill-q1-earnings-call-highlights-2026-11-06/.

findings.finding: On credit cards, a Credit Karma partner-category read: Capital One's Q3 2026 total marketing rose about 14% YoY to about $1.6B, Q4 growth over Q3 is guided similar to 2025, and the CEO plans to 'lean harder into marketing in 2027'. Card-issuer acquisition budgets are expanding (snippet_only; the fetch was blocked).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit Karma revenue +15% to $631M in fiscal Q3 2026. Its FY27 guide is +11-13%, down from about 20%. I found no observed INTU reaction to a Credit Karma surprise.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (Q3 2026 call; page bot-walled, date from snippet context)
findings.why_not_priced: Counterparty commentary rarely makes INTU previews. The 2026-11-17 move was attributed partly to 'consumer credit' worries for Credit Karma's lending partners, which is the opposite of this read. It is a proxy: Credit Karma's share of Capital One's spend is not disclosed.
findings.independence: None for cards. The Upstart read in the next finding points the other way, for loans.

findings.finding: On personal loans, a Credit Karma partner-category read: Upstart's Q3 2026 originations rose 44% YoY to $4.1B, but borrower acquisition costs fell 11% q/q to $91M as Upstart shifted marketing toward its own borrower base. October daily volume fell 9% from September after it tightened credit (still +26% YoY). That is a softer October for marketplace loan referrals.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same as the card read: I found no observed INTU reaction to a Credit Karma surprise. Credit Karma's FY27 guide (+11-13%) already marks a deceleration.
findings.why_not_priced: Upstart did not name Credit Karma. The read-across rests on lower acquisition spend and an October slowdown. Previews do not discuss it, so if it were priced Credit Karma estimates would have been cut, and no such cut is reported.
findings.independence: Capital One's card marketing (the previous finding) points the other way. The two roughly cancel for Credit Karma.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: the stock fell 9.05% in five sessions and 12.83% in twenty, including -5.35% on 2026-11-17 against a sector down 3.84%, with no company-specific catalyst reported. Options price upside: 25-delta skew is -10.85 vol points and put/call open interest is 0.54. Short interest is only about 3% (2.2 days to cover). The bar for the reaction has been lowered, but the option market already pays for the bounce.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-25 the stock was -11.8% premarket on a weak guide and closed only -3.24%, so dip buyers absorbed a bad guide. After the May 2026 print (cuts plus a TurboTax trim) the stock fell 20.02%.
findings.why_not_priced: It largely is priced, which is why the size is small: the skew is the market saying the same thing. The one unpriced element is that a reaffirm-only print starts from $309 rather than the $342 of 2026-11-11.
findings.independence: https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Intuit+Slides+Ahead+of+Earnings+as+Investors+Reassess+Growth+Outlook (2026-11-17) reports a -6.2% day and 'no obvious company-specific catalyst'. The baseline skew is an independent read of the same positioning.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-20 Intuit relaunched Credit Karma Tax with free federal filing for any complexity and $15 state filing. RBC reads it as a fix for the 3 points of DIY share TurboTax lost in FY26, and estimates about 80% of its users are incremental. The FY27 TurboTax guide is +2-3%. The Q1 call is the first chance for management to say whether the launch changes the TurboTax or Consumer outlook or adds spending.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: TurboTax share and pricing drove the May 2026 print (-20.02%, TurboTax forecast trimmed, and the CEO admitted pricing was driving customers away). The FY27 guide on 2026-08-25 was sold (-3.24%).
findings.why_not_priced: The launch is public, but its revenue cost (cannibalisation of paid TurboTax) and its funnel benefit are not quantified anywhere. If either were priced, FY27 TurboTax estimates would have moved off the +2-3% guide, and no such revision is reported. The sign is genuinely ambiguous.
findings.independence: RBC's positive read is summarised at https://finimize.com/content/intuit-looks-to-credit-karma-tax-to-win-back-diy-filers. The CEO's admission on pricing is at https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/intuit-ceo-admits-pricing-is-driving-turbo-tax-customers-away-says-low-cost-fix-coming-as-stock-extends-tumble-overnight/cZYNiVQRJoq.

findings.finding: Street FY27 EPS is $23.49 against the company's $22.88-23.12 guide, about 2% above the top, so the market already expects an EPS raise. Intuit's habit at Q1 is to reiterate the full year, as it did on 2025-11-20. A reaffirm-only print, or a Q2 guide that does not show customer re-acceleration, would undershoot what estimates assume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26: FY reiterated, stock +4.03%. Q4 FY26: the guide fell below consensus, -11.8% premarket and -3.24% at the close. Investor Day 2026-09-17: reaffirm-only, stock -4% and JPMorgan downgraded.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock trades as if it fears a further cut rather than expecting a raise, yet sell-side EPS still sits above the guide. If the market expected a reaffirm, that $23.49 figure would already be at or below $23.12. The gap is small.
findings.independence: The Investor Day reaction to a reaffirm-only is at https://www.tikr.com/blog/intuit-stock-analysis-why-street-sees-34-upside (stock -4%, $303 close on 2026-09-18), a separate document.

outside_window.finding: The TurboTax season effect of Credit Karma Tax's free federal filing (Q3 FY27, February-April 2027) shows up only in tax-season units and revenue.

baseline_tension: What I found leans mildly positive, in agreement with the skew (upside paid) and the five-day drop. That agreement is why the positive findings are small: the market is already positioned for a relief bounce. The one negative, a reaffirm-only against a street EPS above the guide, cuts against the skew.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name's beats were sold when the guide disappointed): Q1 beat finding cut from +0.8 to +0.6.
Lesson 6 (a finding inside what the company already guided): QBO price-increase finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2, because the increase was announced before the guide.
Lesson 7 and lesson 5 (a sign that agrees with the skew is priced; an unexplained drawdown is not evidence): positioning finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3.
Lesson 9 (size a segment finding net of the rest): the two Credit Karma proxies kept small and offsetting, unchanged.
abs_move_pct and p_up were unchanged (8.5 and 55), so expected_move_pct stays +0.85; impact_sum moved from 1.4 to 0.9.
